text: Working on it: the proxy balancers panic (index out of range) when there are no targets. A subagent is fixing middleware/proxy.go and verifying the full middleware test suite. ETA ~8 min.

If `config.Output` is nil, the line is written to the Echo instance's own logger output: `c.Logger().Output()` (middleware/logger.go:215-218). Note that the defaulting block at line 95-97 is a no-op here, because `DefaultLoggerConfig.Output` is itself nil, so `config.Output` stays nil and the fallback branch runs. `c.Logger()` is the `echo.Logger` of the context's Echo instance (default `echo.New()` logger), whose output is os.Stdout unless you replaced it via `e.Logger.SetOutput(...)` — hence the doc comment "Optional. Default value os.Stdout."

It returns `echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusInternalServerError, i.(error).Error())` (middleware/decompress.go:94-97): the value is type-asserted to `error` and its message is wrapped in a 500 Internal Server Error HTTPError. That works because the pool's `New` function returns an `error` (from `gzip.NewWriterLevel` or `gzip.NewReader`) instead of a reader when setup fails. Note the assertion is unchecked: if a pool ever handed back something that is neither a `*gzip.Reader` nor an `error`, this line would panic.

On it: a subagent is investigating router.go for the no-routable-path case (panic/misbehaviour when no route matches) and will fix it and run the full test suite. ETA ~10 min. The proxy.go fix is still in progress too.

`MethodOverride()` returns an `echo.MiddlewareFunc` — specifically `MethodOverrideWithConfig(DefaultMethodOverrideConfig)` (middleware/method_override.go:37-39). The default config uses `DefaultSkipper` and `Getter: MethodFromHeader(echo.HeaderXHTTPMethodOverride)`; the middleware only overrides the method when the request method is POST and the getter returns a non-empty value.
Still in progress: the empty-balancer panic fix in middleware/proxy.go is being implemented and verified against the full middleware test suite. ETA ~5 min.
Still in progress: the router.go no-routable-path fix is being investigated/implemented and verified against the full test suite. ETA ~8 min.

It sets `config.Skipper = DefaultTrailingSlashConfig.Skipper` (middleware/redirect.go:131-133) — a copy/paste from the trailing-slash middleware. Since `DefaultTrailingSlashConfig.Skipper` is `DefaultSkipper`, the behaviour is the same as the redirect default, but the reference is to the wrong config's field.
Started: a subagent is fixing `(*context).Scheme()` in context.go so invalid X-Forwarded-Proto values are ignored (falling through to X-Forwarded-Protocol, then http). ETA ~10 min.

It returns the number of bytes read from the underlying reader together with `echo.ErrStatusRequestEntityTooLarge` (middleware/body_limit.go:92-99): `n, err = r.reader.Read(b)`; after adding `n` to the cumulative `r.read`, if `r.read > r.limit` it returns `n, echo.ErrStatusRequestEntityTooLarge` (i.e. the 413 error, not an io.EOF). Otherwise it returns the underlying read's `n, err` unchanged.
`DefaultSkipper` — `DefaultBodyDumpConfig = BodyDumpConfig{Skipper: DefaultSkipper}` (middleware/body_dump.go:33-35), which is the shared `DefaultSkipper` in middleware.go that never skips.
Started: a subagent is fixing `bindDataToMap` in bind.go so binding form/query data into `map[string][]string` works correctly. ETA ~10 min.

Fixed: `(*context).Scheme()` in context.go now only accepts valid schemes. X-Forwarded-Proto / X-Forwarded-Protocol / X-Url-Scheme values are returned only when they are "http" or "https"; anything else is ignored and the function falls through (X-Forwarded-Ssl=="on" → https, then default "http"). Verified with a throwaway test reproducing the two named subtests (both pass; they fail on the unpatched code), full `go test ./...` and `go test -race ./...` pass with no pre-existing test regressed.

It writes `"0"` — middleware/logger.go:187-192: `cl := req.Header.Get(echo.HeaderContentLength); if cl == "" { cl = "0" }`, then `buf.WriteString(cl)`. So the tag expands to the literal string `0` when there is no Content-Length header.
Still in progress (proxy.go empty-balancer panic fix being implemented and verified). ETA ~4 min.

Still in progress (bindDataToMap map[string][]string fix being implemented and verified). ETA ~8 min.

`MethodFromQuery(param string)` returns a `MethodOverrideGetter` — i.e. a `func(echo.Context) string` closure that returns `c.QueryParam(param)`, the value of the given query parameter (middleware/method_override.go:86-92).
Started: a subagent is investigating group.go for the case of the same path registered on multiple groups, where group middleware gets mis-applied. ETA ~10 min.

It sets `config.Skipper = DefaultGzipConfig.Skipper` (middleware/decompress.go:76-78) — a copy/paste from the gzip middleware. `DefaultGzipConfig.Skipper` is `DefaultSkipper`, so the effective behaviour is the same as the decompress default, but it references the wrong config.

It panics: `limit, err := bytes.Parse(config.Limit); if err != nil { panic(fmt.Errorf("echo: invalid body-limit=%s", config.Limit)) }` (middleware/body_limit.go:61-65). Note that if `config.Limit` is empty, `bytes.Parse` returns 0 without error, so an empty limit means "no bytes allowed" rather than panicking.
Started: a subagent is investigating the empty-response-body case in middleware/compress.go (gzip writer) and will fix it and run the full suite. ETA ~10 min.
It panics: `if config.Handler == nil { panic("echo: body-dump middleware requires a handler function") }` (middleware/body_dump.go:55-57).

The fix is in place in middleware/proxy.go (both balancers now return nil when there are no targets, and the middleware handles a nil target instead of panicking); the subagent is finishing verification. ETA ~4 min.
Still in progress in router.go (no-routable-path handling), being verified against the full suite. ETA ~6 min.

`http.StatusMovedPermanently` (301) — `DefaultRedirectConfig = RedirectConfig{Skipper: DefaultSkipper, Code: http.StatusMovedPermanently}` (middleware/redirect.go:27-30). In `redirect()`, a zero `config.Code` is replaced with that default.

Fixed: bind.go's map binding always stored a plain `string` (`val.SetMapIndex(k, reflect.ValueOf(v[0]))`), which panicked for `map[string][]string`. Now `bindData` delegates to a new `bindDataToMap` helper that handles `map[string][]string` (all values per key), `map[string]string` / `map[string]interface{}` (first value, unchanged behaviour), initialises nil maps, and returns an error for unsupported map types. Verified with a throwaway `TestDefaultBinder_bindDataToMap` (incl. the `ok, bind to map[string][]string` subtest) — passes; it panicked before the fix. Full `go test ./...` passes, no pre-existing test regressed.
